description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Theory of Computation topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: theory-of-computation

facts.claim: Regular ⊂ context-free ⊂ context-sensitive ⊂ recursively enumerable

source.quote: Every regular language is context-free, every context-free language is context-sensitive

facts.claim: Type-0 grammars generate recursively enumerable languages

source.quote: Recursively enumerable (Type-0) grammars

facts.claim: A DFA has exactly one transition per state and symbol

source.quote: Upon reading a symbol, a DFA jumps deterministically from one state to another by following the transition arrow

facts.claim: Finitely many states

source.quote: deterministic finite automaton (DFA)

facts.claim: Every NFA converts to an equivalent DFA (subset construction)

source.quote: Using the subset construction algorithm, each NFA can be translated to an equivalent DFA

facts.claim: Every DFA is also an NFA
facts.pattern: every DFA is (also )?an NFA|DFA is a special case

source.quote: In particular, every DFA is also an NFA

facts.claim: A regular expression specifies a pattern of strings

source.quote: is a sequence of characters that specifies a match pattern in text

facts.claim: Operations: union (|), concatenation and star

source.quote: (alternation) (R|S) denotes the set union of sets described by R and S

facts.claim: Long strings can have a middle part repeated (pumped)

source.quote: all sufficiently long strings in a regular language may be pumped

facts.claim: Used to prove a language is not regular

source.quote: The pumping lemma is useful for proving that a specific language is not a regular language

facts.claim: Each production replaces a single nonterminal

source.quote: can be applied to a nonterminal symbol regardless of its context

facts.claim: Rules produce strings of terminals and nonterminals

source.quote: a string of terminals and/or nonterminals

facts.claim: A pushdown automaton uses a stack

source.quote: a type of automaton that employs a stack

facts.claim: NPDAs recognise exactly the context-free languages

source.quote: nondeterministic ones can recognize all context-free languages

facts.claim: An infinite tape divided into cells, read by a head

source.quote: The machine operates on an infinite memory tape divided into discrete cells

facts.claim: It follows a table of rules (transition function)

source.quote: manipulates symbols on a strip of tape according to a table of rules

facts.claim: Effectively calculable = computable by a Turing machine

source.quote: a function on the natural numbers can be calculated by an effective method if and only if it is computable by a Turing machine

facts.claim: Decidable: an effective method always gives the right yes/no answer

source.quote: a true/false decision problem is decidable if there exists an effective method for deriving the correct answer

facts.claim: Many important problems are undecidable

source.quote: Many important problems are undecidable

facts.claim: Ambiguous: some string has more than one parse tree / leftmost derivation

source.quote: there exists a string that can have more than one leftmost derivation or parse tree

facts.claim: All non-trivial semantic properties of programs are undecidable

source.quote: all non-trivial semantic properties of programs are undecidable

facts.claim: Semantic = about the program's behaviour, not its syntax

source.quote: A semantic property is one about the program's behavior
